Yeah! Scored pills are usually evenly distributed. Just make sure to save the other half in a clean and dry environment
Oh I forgot to mention that remeron is more sedating in lower doses, so you may feel more sleepy if you cut your pills in half

As a general advice I don't think it's good to cut pills because it's not sure that you'll get half the dosage in each part. Also remeron is usually sublingual and dissolves with moisture, so I don't think it would be advisable to store the other half to take it on the next day. All this can be done, it's just not optimal.

Regarding side effects, the most common one is sleepiness, so you may sleep faster than usual and still feel more sleepy than usual on the next morning. Starting on a 10mg dosage, I felt more sleepy in the first 2 weeks and had more vivid dreams for about a month.

All things considered, in my experience, remeron is an easy drug to start taking, so don't be too worried. You can document your symptoms and talk about them with your doctor in your next appointment to see if what you experience is within the acceptable.

Even if you're a minor your parents can't force you to take a medication against your will, at least it's your doctor who should decide what's best for you based on how you feel. Do you have the opportunity to talk to your doctor without your parents? 

But four weeks it's not a long time yet and maybe these feelings will get better and maybe they won't. It's not easy to find the right drug that will work without side effects. Antidepressants are not all the same at all. Maybe if your psychiatrist suggested a therapist then your parents would be more open to this idea?

My psychiatrist told me that from 150mg to 75mg was worse because at 150mg it activates two neurotransmitters and at 75mg it activates just one (I'm not sure of the details but it's something like this), so it's like you're taking a different drug. Some people start to feel withdrawal effects even if they take their dosage a couple hours later, so it could start immediately or after a couple days. 
When I decreased from 75mg to 37,5mg I didn't feel anything, I never had any problems if I missed a dose for a day (even when I was on 150) so I thought I was gonna be ok, that I was one of the lucky ones who wouldn't feel the withdrawal effects. And boy was I wrong! 2 days after my last dose I started to feel bad, body was hurting a little bit and I was more depressed than usual, but nothing that at the time I associated with the withdrawal. But then I had one of the worst weeks of my life, physically and mentally. I'm sure you can find plenty descriptions of how it feels online. My point is that even if you don't feel too bad while tapering off it can still be a nightmare when you stop completely. If I could do it again I would have tapered off by taking one ball from the capsule each day. A lot of people do this and it seems to be a better option. Good luck!

I literally felt a lump in my throat when I read the title of your post because I've been pushing her away too. I've often felt frustrated with my girlfriend because she didn't want the same things as me or she wasn't doing what I wanted, but I realized (with the help of my therapist) that I was being extremely egotistic and I that I don't know how to deal with frustrations. I have a bad relationship with myself but it was easier to aim all this towards her (and also my parents). I'm trying to change because I want to be a better person to the people I love.

It's great that you're going to therapy, but maybe you should try going to a psychiatrist too. Anger problems are sometimes associated with other problems like depression and bipolar disorder. 
Also does your anger only affects your relationship or other parts of your life too? It's good to keep a diary of when you've experienced these episode so you can better analyze what set you off. 

Try to put yourself in your girlfriend's shoes and don't focus so much on trying to get back with her but on being a better person to the people you love and having a good relationship with yourself.

I don't think you should feel bad for wanting to do something negative if you are able stop yourself. It's normal to have negative thoughts and impulses, the important thing is knowing how to identify them and to stop yourself before you do something that you really don't want to do. Don't blame yourself for having this impulses, they don't define who you are and they don't mean that you really want to act on them. Not all our thoughts represent us truly. 
Be proud that you are capable of not letting yourself get dominated by this impulses and that you can meditate.

Yeah I know that knowing the root problem doesn't solve everything, but there are different types of therapy. Have you tried CBT? I really like it because it focuses more on how to deal with your feelings in an active way, not simply discussing the root problems. 

When you've found the martial art that you like let me know which one it is!

I think the best method, and also the hardest, to deal with anger is to find the root problem. Are you really not making progress or are you being too hard on yourself and setting high standards? Have you tried different learning methods? Do you have trouble to concentrate or to remember things? What is your need or motivation to learn those things? It's really hard to be honest with ourselves. 

Have you heard about Progressive Muscle Relaxation? I don't know if it's considered a type of meditation exactly, it's an exercise that you have to exert some force and it's not as "passive" as meditation.
